findings.title: [resolved] Non-canonical pull_request_url re-send no longer resets custom title (WARN->PASS)

confidence.rationale: Title-clear heuristic now compares the normalized pullRequestURL to ch.PullRequestURL; the SQLite trailing-slash regression test executes the exact edge and asserts the custom title is preserved.

findings.symptom: (prior) A client re-sending pull_request_url equal to the stored PR in non-canonical form (trailing slash / whitespace) with no title reset the custom title to the derived default. (resolved) The heuristic now compares the normalized/canonical URL to the stored canonical URL, so equivalent URLs do not trigger a title clear.
findings.source: apps/api/internal/store/sqlite/mutations.go and apps/api/internal/store/postgres/mutations.go — `pullRequestURL, _, err = store.NormalizePullRequestContext(pullRequestURL, "")` runs before `if input.PullRequestTitle == nil && pullRequestURL != ch.PullRequestURL { pullRequestTitle = "" }` (the comparison now uses the normalized URL, not the raw pre-normalization input as in the prior artifact).
findings.consequence: Custom human-readable PR titles are preserved across a no-op equivalent-URL re-send with cosmetic variation. URL data was never lost; the derived-title reset is now eliminated for trailing-slash and whitespace variation.
findings.remedy: Applied in this regen cycle: normalize the candidate URL before the equality check. No further action required.
findings.verification: go test -count=1 -run 'ChannelPresentation' ./apps/api/internal/store/sqlite/ -> ok; the test sets pullRequestURL + custom title, re-sends pullRequestURL+"/" with no title, and asserts updated.PullRequestURL==pullRequestURL && updated.PullRequestTitle==pullRequestTitle.
findings.resolution: Resolved in staged tree dd1b7deb; title-clear now compares canonical URL. SQLite trailing-slash regression test added and passing.

findings.title: [resolved] OpenAPI now declares uri-reference and canonical GitHub PR pattern for pull_request_url (WARN->PASS)

confidence.rationale: OpenAPI UpdateChannelRequest.pull_request_url now declares format: uri-reference, a pattern matching the server constraint, and a description; the schema-vs-server surprise gap is closed for canonical lowercase URLs.

findings.symptom: (prior) OpenAPI declared pull_request_url as an unconstrained string while the server rejected non-canonical URLs with 400, surprising schema-conformant clients. (resolved) The schema now declares format: uri-reference, pattern '^$|^https://github\.com/[^/]+/[^/]+/pull/[1-9][0-9]*$', and a description to clear the context, matching the server's NormalizePullRequestContext acceptance rule for canonical lowercase URLs.
findings.source: packages/protocol/openapi.yaml UpdateChannelRequest.pull_request_url (format: uri-reference; pattern: '^$|^https://github\.com/[^/]+/[^/]+/pull/[1-9][0-9]*$'; description: 'Canonical HTTPS github.com pull request URL for this code channel. Send an empty string to clear it.') vs apps/api/internal/store/types.go NormalizePullRequestContext.
findings.consequence: Schema-conformant clients sending a canonical https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/pull/{n} URL (or empty string to clear) no longer hit an undocumented 400. The schema documents the server constraint.
findings.remedy: Applied in this regen cycle: add format/pattern/description to the OpenAPI field. No further action required for the canonical case.
findings.verification: Cross-checked OpenAPI UpdateChannelRequest.pull_request_url constraints against NormalizePullRequestContext acceptance; pattern accepts the canonical form and the empty clear-string, and rejects http/example.com/issues/non-numeric URLs, consistent with the server for canonical lowercase input.
findings.resolution: Resolved in staged tree dd1b7deb; OpenAPI declares uri-reference + canonical GitHub PR pattern.
findings.residualNote: The pattern is marginally stricter than the server (rejects uppercase host and leading-zero numbers the server accepts via EqualFold/atoi); this is the safe direction and does not reintroduce the F-2 surprise. Recorded as info, not a new low finding.
